alerts.title: "I sent you money by mistake, please send it back"
alerts.summary: You get what looks like a money confirmation, then a call or SMS begging you to return the money. No money ever arrived: the confirmation came from an ordinary phone number, not from M-PESA or MoMo.
alerts.example: TFX4K2 Confirmed. Ksh2,500.00 received from PETER M 0722000111. Nimekosea kutuma, tafadhali rudisha.
spot: Real M-PESA and MoMo messages come from the name M-PESA or MoMo, never from a 07… number
Your balance didn't actually go up
They're in a hurry and keep calling
do: Check your real balance with the official menu before doing anything
Never send money back yourself. A real mistake is reversed by the provider
In Kenya, forward the fake SMS to 333

alerts.title: "Please send me the code I just sent you"
alerts.summary: A stranger, or a hacked friend, asks for a code that just arrived by SMS. That code lets them take over your WhatsApp, your mobile money or your bank account.
alerts.example: Hi, I sent a 6-digit code to your number by mistake. Can you send it to me? It's urgent.
spot: Nobody legitimate ever needs a code that was sent to you
The code's own SMS usually says "don't share this code"
Messages from a friend's account that suddenly ask for codes or money
do: Never share a code, even with someone who sounds like customer care
Turn on two-step verification in WhatsApp (Settings › Account)
Call your friend on their usual number to check

alerts.title: Fake customer care calls
alerts.summary: A caller says they're from your mobile network or bank. Your line will be blocked, your account is frozen or you've won a reward, unless you "confirm" your PIN or dial a code they give you.
alerts.example: Hello, this is customer care. Your line will be suspended today. Please dial the code I'll give you to keep it active.
spot: Real staff never ask for your PIN or password
They call from an ordinary mobile number
They want you to act right now, while on the call
do: Hang up and call the official customer care number yourself
Never dial codes or install apps a caller asks you to
Block the number in ScottPrivacy and tap Report as scam so others are warned

alerts.title: "You've won" promotions with a fee
alerts.summary: An SMS says you won cash, airtime or a phone in an anniversary promotion. To claim it you must pay a "registration" or "delivery" fee, or open a link.
alerts.example: Congratulations! You have won Ksh 50,000 in the anniversary promotion. Pay Ksh 300 registration fee to claim.
spot: You never entered any competition
Real prizes never ask you to pay first
Links to odd websites instead of the company's official one
do: Don't pay and don't open the link
Paste the message into ScottPrivacy's checker to see the warning signs
Delete it or move it to Spam

alerts.title: "Earn money liking videos" and online job offers
alerts.summary: A friendly stranger on WhatsApp or Telegram offers easy pay for liking videos or rating products. The first small payments are real. Then you're asked to "top up" to unlock bigger tasks, and the money is gone.
alerts.example: Hello! We are hiring part-time. Earn 3,000 daily by liking YouTube videos. Reply YES to start.
spot: Jobs that find you out of nowhere
Pay that's far too high for simple tasks
Any request to deposit money to earn money
do: Never pay to get a job or unlock tasks
Stop replying and block the sender
Warn friends and family: this one spreads fast

alerts.title: Parcel waiting, pay a small fee
alerts.summary: An SMS says a parcel couldn't be delivered and asks you to pay a small customs or delivery fee through a link. The link steals your card or mobile money details.
alerts.example: Your parcel is on hold due to unpaid customs fee of 150. Pay now to avoid return: http://parcel-release.top/pay
spot: You're not expecting a parcel
Strange web addresses, often with .top, .xyz or lots of numbers
Tiny fee and a short deadline
do: Don't open the link
Track parcels only on the courier's official website or app
If you entered card details, call your bank straight away

alerts.title: "Enter your UPI PIN to receive money"
alerts.summary: Someone, often a "buyer" on a selling site, sends you a UPI collect request and says you'll receive money by approving it. Entering your UPI PIN always sends money out, never in.
alerts.example: I've sent the payment request for your sofa. Just approve it on your UPI app and enter your PIN to receive the money.
spot: You never need a PIN to receive money
Collect requests from people you don't know
Pressure to approve quickly
do: Decline the request
Report fraud at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930
Report fake calls and SMS on Sanchar Saathi (sancharsaathi.gov.in)

alerts.title: "Update your KYC or your account will be blocked"
alerts.summary: An SMS says your bank account, wallet or SIM will be blocked today unless you update your KYC through a link or an app. The link or app steals your details or takes over your phone.
alerts.example: Dear customer, your account will be blocked today. Update KYC now: http://kyc-update-bank.xyz
spot: Banks don't block accounts through a link in an SMS
Requests to install an app to "update" anything
Threats and same-day deadlines
do: Don't open the link or install anything
Visit your bank's branch or official app to check
Never install screen-sharing apps because a caller asks
